The Turtle That Had Been Put in the Wrong Pond

被放进了错误水池的龟 · 648 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1An aquarium took in a turtle after a coastal flood. The rescue card called it a marine creature, so an assistant prepared a saltwater tank. A young biologist named Fen looked at its slender claws and a green mark on its shell. She had seen the same mark on freshwater turtles in a tidal marsh. If the card was wrong, a tank meant for oceanic species might harm it. Fen asked the keeper to wait while she found the animal's original habitat.

2They checked the wildlife center's map. One trail went to a bay where a dolphin and a whale had been seen. Fishermen there caught tuna, squid, and crab. A separate channel led to a pond with lilies, frogs, and nesting ducks. A pair of geese used its muddy bank. The driver thought his photograph showed sand from the bay. Fen enlarged it and saw a leaf caught against the animal's claw. It looked like a marsh lily rather than a plant from the shore.

3The center had once used a separate sign for each migration route. It showed where salmon returned from the sea and where a goose might land. A child thought the turtle could move from pond to bay in the same way. Fen asked him to look at the markings. A group of fish could migrate between different waters. A damaged rescue label gave no evidence that this animal could.

4A footprint lay beside the turtle. A hunter thought it belonged to a lizard. Fen measured its shape. A snake would leave a longer track, a crocodile a wider one. A rat or a young mammal might leave separate marks. The picture also showed wet ink on a piece of bark. A volunteer had painted nest covers to record where eggs hatched. He asked staff to keep bait away. One cover broke and drifted with the tide. It could have drifted from another habitat.

5Fen followed the number to a gate. The keeper remembered a parrot cage and a pet carrier used that afternoon. A child gave him a hamster box with a wet label, containing a turtle. He moved it into a stronger carrier and accidentally copied a label from an octopus rescued from a marine display. A whole section of the aquarium had been evacuated. A mismatch could send a freshwater inhabitant beside a lobster or a shark without anyone doing it deliberately.

6They still had to find where the turtle could thrive. An environmentalist checked for destructive invasive species. A fallen branch lay across a frog's nest. Pigeons settled near the food people left, and a few mice came out of a hole. A dove flew past a swallow near the bank. A wasp and butterflies found nourishment among the dry flowers. A local goat herder said his flock drank farther upstream. These signs showed where wildlife could inhabit the bank without being fed by visitors.

7A volunteer wanted to release the turtle immediately. Fen asked a vet to check whether a sick animal could infect the wild population. A tick or flea on a stray pet would be a different concern from a torn shell on a wild turtle. A photograph showed the same green mark on an animal that used to breed near the gate. The keeper chose a quiet spot away from geese and marked it so that nobody would disturb the turtle before it could dive or feed.

8A child asked how an aquarium could show where a turtle belonged. Fen compared a pond label with one from a polar display. A penguin, a goldfish, and a marsh turtle could all swim. They needed different surroundings. A feather on the wrong crate could be as misleading as the copied label. In the ecology room the visitor matched the leaf to the pond on a map of the continent. She traced the journey without listing every animal.

四级汇总词汇 · 28中文译文

被放进了错误水池的龟

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1沿海洪水后，水族馆接收了一只龟。救助卡把它写成海洋动物，助手便准备海水缸。年轻生物学家芬看见它细长的爪和龟壳上的绿印。她在潮汐沼泽的淡水龟身上也见过同样的记号。如果卡片错了，给海洋物种用的水缸会伤到它。芬请饲养员先等她找到原栖息地。

2他们查看野生动物中心的地图。一条路通往见过海豚和鲸的海湾，渔民在那里捉金枪鱼、鱿鱼和螃蟹。另一条水道通向有百合、青蛙和筑巢野鸭的池塘，两只鹅常在泥岸上。司机觉得照片上的沙来自海湾。芬把照片放大，在龟爪边看见一片叶。它像沼泽里的百合叶，和海岸植物不一样。

3中心过去给每条迁徙路线立不同的牌子，标出鲑鱼从哪儿回到淡水，鹅又会在哪里落脚。孩子觉得龟也能从池塘照样游到海湾。芬请他看具体标记。有些鱼会在不同水域之间迁徙。一张损坏的标签却不足以证明这只龟也能那么做。

4龟旁有个脚印。有人说像蜥蜴的，芬量了形状。蛇留下的痕迹会更长，鳄鱼的会更宽，老鼠或小哺乳动物可能留下几个分开的印子。图里一块树皮上还有湿墨。志愿者曾给巢盖写编号，记录哪里孵出了蛋，也请工作人员不要放诱饵。其中一个盖子坏了，随潮水漂动，可能来自另一片栖息地。

5芬循着编号走到门边。饲养员记得那天下午用过鹦鹉笼和宠物提箱。一个孩子拿来标签淋湿的仓鼠盒，里面装的却是龟。他把龟换进结实的箱子时，无意抄了另一张标签，那张原本属于从海洋展区救出来的章鱼。水族馆有整片区域撤空，一个误配的标签就可能让淡水居民被送到龙虾和鲨鱼旁边。

6他们还得找出龟能好好生活的地方。环保人员查有没有破坏性的外来物种。一根落枝横在蛙巢上。鸽子在残余食物边停留，几只老鼠钻出洞。岸边，一只鸽子飞过燕子附近，黄蜂和蝴蝶在旱地的花里找食物。牧羊人说，他的山羊到上游喝水。这些迹象显示，哪里的野生动物不靠游人喂食也能生活。

7志愿者想立即放龟。芬请兽医先查它会不会把病传给野外种群。流浪宠物身上的蜱或跳蚤，和野龟壳裂开是不同的问题。一张老照片显示，以前在门边繁殖的一只龟也有这个绿印。饲养员选了远离鹅群的安静处，标明位置，免得龟还没来得及下潜或进食就被打扰。

8有孩子问，水族馆怎么展示龟原来住哪儿。芬拿池塘的标签和极地展的标签对照。企鹅、金鱼和沼泽龟都会游，却需要不同环境。箱子上恰好沾一根羽毛，也可能像抄错的标签一样误导人。在生态展厅，访客把叶子和大陆地图上的池塘对应起来。她可以沿着路线讲下去，不用把所有动物逐一背出来。
